QF.id: AIFM Fee Structure and Fund Performance_15

question.text: Unlike operating expenses, Transaction Expenses (brokerage, depository, custodian transaction charges, STT, exchange charges) for an AIF are:

answer.text: Paid only from the incentive fee pool
Absorbed entirely by the Investment Manager
Borne on actuals without any limit

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that transaction expenses for an AIF are borne on an actual basis without any limit. The named transaction costs include brokerage, depository charges, custodian transaction charges, STT and exchange charges. The Trap: Option A confuses transaction expenses with the operating-expense cap. Option B mixes separate fee pools. Option C shifts the burden to the manager, which is not how the workbook treats these costs. Note: The key distinction from operating expenses is that transaction expenses have no cap and follow the listed cost categories.
